Soporific

sop-uh-RIF-ik · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Soporific is tending to induce drowsiness or sleep.

The lecture hall grew quieter and quieter as the professor's soporific monotone droned on, until half the students were nodding off.

Worked Example

The warm cabin, the gentle rocking of the train, and the soporific hum of the engine combined to make it almost impossible to stay awake.

Soporific describes anything -- a voice, a warm room, a dull book -- that makes you sleepy, whether or not it's literally a sleeping pill.

How Soporific Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

sedative

sedative: having a calming, sleep-inducing effect

somnolent

somnolent: sleepy or drowsy

Antonyms

invigorating

invigorating: energizing and refreshing

exhilarating

exhilarating: thrilling and exciting

How Strong Is It? — relaxing → soporific → narcotic

relaxing vs. soporific

relaxing vs. soporific: Relaxing describes mild calm, without necessarily making you sleepy the way soporific does.

narcotic vs. soporific

narcotic vs. soporific: Narcotic describes a substance so powerful it can produce unconsciousness, far beyond ordinary drowsiness.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — sopor

root — sopor: deep sleep (Latin)

suffix — -ific

suffix — -ific: making, causing (Latin -ficus, from facere 'to make')

Put it together

Put it together: Soporific comes from Latin sopor ('deep sleep') + -ific ('making, causing') -- literally 'sleep-making.' Anything soporific is something that makes you sleepy.

Use the root in a new word: soporose

Use the root in a new word: soporose: Doctors sometimes use the rare medical term soporose to describe a patient in an unnaturally deep, sleep-like state.

Word Building

Word Choice

Soporific works for literal sleep-inducers (a pill, warm milk) and, just as often, for anything so boring it makes you drowsy -- a droning lecture, a dense contract.
